title: Request lifecycle throttle: policy templates and escalation playbook
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Implement a request lifecycle-based throttling system with reusable policy templates and an operator-facing escalation playbook to reduce P99 latency breaches during region failover and spikes.
description: Background: Incidents over the past 18 months show repeated P99 latency breaches during regional failover and bursty tenant traffic. Existing admission controllers are effective but fragmented: different services use ad-hoc token buckets, static lane counts, or model-specific truncation. This ticket aims to create a unified request-lifecycle throttle that: (1) applies policy templates at the API gateway and runtime admission layer, (2) coordinates graceful degradation actions across priority queues, KV cache rehydration, and output fidelity transforms, and (3) exposes a clear escalation playbook for SREs and on-call engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Policy templates implemented and stored in config service; at least three templates: conservative, balanced, aggressive
Gateway admission integrates with runtime controller and can return standard degradation responses (HTTP 429 with 'X-Redwood-Fallback' header) within 20ms of decision
Control-plane API to toggle templates per-region and per-tenant with audit logs
Automated escalation playbook document available in Confluence with runbook steps, metrics to watch, and rollback actions
End-to-end tests simulating multi-region failover show <5% additional error rate and under 10% token-cost increase compared to baseline while restoring 95th-percentile latency within 60s
design_notes: We favor a short stateless decision layer at the gateway that emits a compact policy token; runtime controllers make final admission using token + local occupancy
Avoid global coordination at the hot path; use soft-signals (region health tags + tenant recent-burst-score) propagated through request headers

Graceful degradation actions ordered by lowest customer-impact first: 1) prefix cache reuse, 2) request batching window expansion up to configured max, 3) structured output trimming (remove non-essential fields), 4) model variant fallback
Trade-off: aggressive template reduces p99 quickly but increases hallucination risk if model fallback used; include quality-monitoring hook to flag regressions
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Policy schema and template CRUD in config service (Config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/configs/pull/1424)
Phase 2: Gateway decision service + token header (Gateway PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/981)
Phase 3: Runtime controller hook to interpret template token and run admission (Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2706)
Phase 4: Confluence runbook and on-call playbook, run a staged game-day exercise across us-east/us-west/eu-central
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff — scoped to admission path + operator playbook. Decided to centralize templates in configs service. (Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01UNKY/archives/PLAYS-123)
2026-03-04: Prototype of 'balanced' template implemented; initial synthetic load test reduced P99 by ~18% but increased tokens by 6% (benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/invoice/boards/347)

2026-03-07: Design review with Runtime and Console teams. Agreed to add 'X-Redwood-Fallback' header format and standard 429 payload schema. Action: Runtime to add header pass-through. (Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RELF/Request+Lifecycle+Throttle)

2026-03-10: Gateway PR opened for token emission. Found edge case where client libraries expecting raw streaming responses need backward compatible 101 handling — created sub-issue ENG-827407 to track client lib patch
comments: PM (Jordan Patel): Ensure templates support tenant opt-outs for enterprise customers that purchased full-fidelity SLAs.
Design (Aisha Kumar): For structured-trimming rules, include a canonical field-level importance score to avoid dropping security-relevant metadata.
SRE (Ravi Singh): During multi-region failover runbook, add step to temporarily enlarge KV cache TTLs to speed rehydration rather than fall back immediately to lower-fidelity models.
notes: We should treat policy templates as first-class product primitives — allow product and sales to craft tenant-specific templates for enterprise SLA tiers.
Operator playbook must include explicit thresholds for automatic template escalation (example: if region p99 > 2x SLO for 2 consecutive minutes, switch to 'conservative' template and page)
